newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Wednesday:

Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said the Commission had not finished its meeting at lunchtime and that it would continue work in the afternoon. Van der Pas said he would brief journalists on remaining points on the agenda (part time work directive and genetically modified organisms labelling) at 1600/1400 GMT.
Van der Pas said the Commission had adopted a proposal laying down detailed rules for the transport of meat and bone meal.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/673: Preferential arrangements: the Commission proposes improvements.
- IP/97/674: Commission prepares for International Monetary Fund taking powers regarding capital movements.
- IP/97/678: Statement by Jacques Santer on Northern Ireland.
- IP/97/679: The European Commission renews the Scientific Committees in the field of consumer health and food safety.
- IP/97/681: Commission adopts a communication on the social and labour market dimension of the information society "People first - the next steps".
- IP/97/684: Commission decides on controls on the movement of meat and bone meal between Member States.
- IP/97/685: The European Commission encourages the use of the euro symbol.
- Speech/97/162: Speech by Commissioner Hans van den Broek at the Donor Pledging Conference in support of Bosnia Herzegovina.
